svg.title: The Gaza ledger: what Washington notified against what Gaza needs
svg.desc: A bilingual proportional comparison of four figures on Gaza's financing as of 20 August 2026. Gaza's assessed reconstruction need is upwards of 71 billion dollars over five years, according to the joint World Bank, United Nations and European Union assessment published on 20 April 2026, of which housing alone accounts for more than 16 billion dollars across 371,888 damaged or destroyed homes. Board of Peace member states pledged 17 billion dollars at the inaugural meeting in Washington on 19 February 2026. About one per cent of those pledges had been transferred as of 20 May 2026, roughly 170 million dollars on that arithmetic. The State Department notified Congress on 30 July 2026 of 206 million dollars for the International Stabilization Force, reported by Reuters on 19 August 2026. The lower panel sets out what the 206 million dollars buys: 200 million for the force's equipment, infrastructure, vehicles and operating costs, and 6 million to repurpose nine armoured personnel carriers first destined for Nepal, with Albania and Kosovo as the first recipients.
svg.text: The Gaza ledger: the force is funded, the houses are not
